title: Case K — 9 x 9 cube array, point source
summary: 9 x 9 array of 0.06 m cubes with a tracer point source on the floor between rows 2 and 3: velocity and tracer concentration at 203 points in the streets and over the first rows.

configuration.array: 9 rows (along x) by 9 columns (across y) of cubes, H = 0.06 m, pitch 0.12 m (street width = H, plan area ratio 25 %); the pitch is read from the MP drawings
configuration.U_H_note: stated by the readme and data paper; the approach-flow file (Case H's) gives 2.24 m/s at z = 0.06 m
measurement_planes: five heights from 4 mm to 70 mm; the three upper heights only on y = 0 and +-H
configuration.source: 5 mm floor outlet at (-0.15, 0, 0), between rows 2 and 3 on the centre line; 100 % ethylene, 3.6e-6 m3/s
configuration.concentration_normalisation: c0 = q / (U_H H^2) = 429.18 ppm with the cube's H and U_H; the legacy workbook uses H = 0.2 m and UH = 4.94 m/s instead (C0 = 18.218 ppm), see known issues
configuration.instrument: split-fibre hot wire (velocity), high-speed hydrocarbon analyser (concentration), 1000 Hz with a 200 Hz low-pass filter, 60 s per point
configuration.tunnel: Eiffel-type wind tunnel, Tokyo Polytechnic University (Atsugi); 1.2 m wide, 1.0 m high
configuration.scale_note: model scale; the sources state no model:full scale ratio

frame.origin: bottom centre of the windward wall of the 4th row of the central column: x = 0 is that wall, y = 0 the centre line of the central column
frame.x: +x streamwise (the wind blows toward +x); row k spans x in [0.12 (k-4), 0.12 (k-4) + 0.06], so the array spans x in [-0.36, 0.66]
frame.y: +y lateral; column centres at y = 0, +-0.12, ... +-0.48 (the array spans y in [-0.51, 0.51])

inflow_fit.method: least squares, kappa = 0.41, z = 0.02 .. 0.6 m (10 H) on AF_caseK.csv: the profile is Case H's, tabulated for a 0.2 m building, so the window is a choice
inflow_fit.note: the file is the approach flow of Case H (identical rows); the workbook normalises it with uH = U(0.2 m) = 3.23 m/s and H = 0.2 m

fit.method: least squares, kappa = 0.41, z = 0.02 .. 0.6 m (10 H) on AF_caseK.csv: the profile is Case H's, tabulated for a 0.2 m building, so the window is a choice
fit.note: the file is the approach flow of Case H (identical rows); the workbook normalises it with uH = U(0.2 m) = 3.23 m/s and H = 0.2 m

benchmark_data.note: the measured profile and the fit of it are the benchmark's data as cleaned here; everything under `recommended` is a choice

recommended.status: RECOMMENDED by this repository (not part of the benchmark): a log-law inlet fitted to the case's own approach-flow file, with k and epsilon from the standard neutral ABL relations. Any inlet may be submitted; say which in submission.yaml
recommended.profile: U(z) = u*/kappa ln((z + z0)/z0); k = u*^2 / sqrt(Cmu); epsilon = u*^3 / (kappa (z + z0))
recommended.fit: least squares, kappa = 0.41, z = 0.02 .. 0.6 m (10 H) on AF_caseK.csv: the profile is Case H's, tabulated for a 0.2 m building, so the window is a choice
recommended.openfoam: atmBoundaryLayerInletVelocity / atmBoundaryLayerInletK / atmBoundaryLayerInletEpsilon with Uref, Zref, z0 and d = 0; nutkAtmRoughWallFunction with the same z0 on the ground: cases/{id}/inflow_openfoam.txt holds them

flow_direction.meaning: +x is along the wind at WD = 0: flowDir (1 0 0); another WD rotates it about +z by the case's rotation sense (frame.wind_direction_rotation)

inflow.domain: the extents, blockage and cell sizes of Eddy3D's domains are not in its snapshots and are not stated here; mesh.cells and the scale are, where the snapshot has them

probes.columns_meaning: the key columns of a scored file (point_id with config, campaign, instrument, run and wind_direction_deg as the case has them), x, y, z in m (case frame), and scored_as: the families the row is scored in (vector, k, thermistor_bracket, concentration, theta, joined by +)

scored_as.vector: U, V, W and the speed |U| against the split-fibre, LDV or hot-wire components (velocity.U, velocity.V, velocity.W, speed)
scored_as.thermistor_bracket: a mean scalar speed (thermistor, cup or sonic anemometer) against |U| (vs.vector) and sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) (vs.scalar)

scoring.conventions: velocities and the speed over U_ref, k over U_ref^2 (Cases E, F and G publish ratios already); U, V, W, |U| and the thermistor bracket scored as signed velocities (FAC2's ratio keeps the sign; hit rate D = 0.25, W = 0.05); k by the plain definitions (D = 0.25 only); a thermistor, cup or sonic reading (a mean scalar speed) scored against |U| (vs.vector) and sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) (vs.scalar), the two ends of its bracket; c* = C/c0 with one detection limit per case, 1e-3 of the largest measured value; theta = (T_floor - T)/(T_floor - T_H) scored like a positive velocity. The same conventions score the served Eddy3D results (docs/validation/method.md).
scoring.tool: uv run python validation/score_submissions.py <folder>, from a checkout of the repository (pyproject.toml)

metric_meaning.MeanObserved: mean of the measured, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.MeanPredicted: mean of the modelled, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.Fb: fractional bias, 2 (mean_obs - mean_pred) / (mean_obs + mean_pred); positive = model low
metric_meaning.Fac2: fraction of points within a factor of two (harsh near zero for sign-changing V and W)
metric_meaning.HitRate: fraction of points within D = 0.25 relative or W = 0.05 U_H absolute
metric_meaning.GeometricPairs: pairs with both values positive (used for Mg/Vg)
metric_meaning.null: a metric that is undefined for the data (for example Mg and Vg when no pair has both values positive; Fb, Nmse and Nad of a signed velocity component of Case H or I whose observed and predicted means are not both positive)

known_issues: The legacy workbook normalises with H = 0.2 m (Case H's building), UH = 4.94009 m/s and C0 = 18.218 ppm, not the cube's H = 0.06 m and U_H = 2.33 m/s; its normalised columns are 23.6 times smaller in concentration. The API's concentration_ratio uses the cube's c0 = 429.18 ppm.
RS_caseK.csv has no point numbers; point_id is the row order of the file.
The published CSV is the workbook rounded (3 decimals, concentrations 2), with k recomputed from the rounded rms values; the table is rebuilt from the workbook.
AF_caseK.csv is Case H's approach-flow file, row for row (x = -0.493 m, tabulated for a 0.2 m building); it gives 2.24 m/s at z = 0.06 m against the stated U_H = 2.33.
The lateral velocity V is dominated by a cross-flow offset (about 0.06 m/s, also in the empty tunnel); the +y and -y halves cannot confirm its sign.
The mean concentration is not mirror-symmetric (the +y and -y values of one point differ by 44 % on average), so the mirror pairs are not a repeatability estimate; velocity and k are (3 % and 5 %).
The workbook's <usc> / sigma_usc ('velocity magnitude', never below |U|) is not in the table.
Data paper section 3.11 describes the measurements as 'approximately 30 points at eight heights downwind of the line source'; Case K has 203 points at five heights and a point source.
Workbook units: x and y in millimetres in both data sheets; z in millimetres in 'Measurement data' but metres in 'Inflow'.
